scope: Focused diagnostic of current KDE Kicker search focus and category hover in a disposable private Wayland/KWin fixture.

method.environment: Private KWin --virtual Wayland session, active QQuickView host, actual installed Kicker QML copied into isolated XDG data, disposable Plasmoid singleton shim, authenticated org_kde_kwin_fake_input client.
method.search_focus_run: run5 opened the native Kicker representation, waited for deferred focus, sent an initial keyboard sequence before clicking the search field, and then confirmed the text in the field.
method.hover_run: run9 used one authenticated fake-input client for launcher click and pointer motion to the first native category; no second click was sent after opening.
method.focused_result: Search activeFocus became true after the popup opened and the pre-click text sequence was received. In the hover run the category list reported containsMouse=true, childDialog.visible=true, menuVisible=true, and popup.active=true.
method.cleanup: Both private KWin/QQuickView processes exited; cleanup.json lists only the fixture PIDs.

fixture_limits: This is not the production plasmashell panel: a QQuickView hosts Kicker and a test-only Plasmoid singleton supplies shell properties.
The copied QML adds diagnostic aliases only; no production source was edited.
The focused run proves this input path in the fixture, not the user's full Wayland desktop behavior or human acceptance.
The broad applications suite's RESULTADO is not used: this focused run intentionally did not execute its unrelated pin/catalog checks.
conclusion: The focused private fixture opened the current Kicker menu, deferred focus reached its search field without a prior field click, and a category hover opened a child submenu while the popup remained visible. This does not justify another production QML change by itself. P01 remains open for the user's live-session review and any remaining criteria.
